studies.title: How 274 FLEX droplet fires ended
studies.what: 274 droplet tests. 186 Extinction, 61 Disruption, 27 Completion. Fuels in the table: Methanol, Heptane. Oxygen spans 12% to 34%. 123 tests record a CO-column diluent above zero. 50 record helium above zero.

studies.title: Pressure decides how much of a droplet a cool flame burns
studies.what: Extinction diameter is how big the droplet still is when its flame goes out. In the measurements, raising pressure from 0.5 to 3 atm takes the cool-flame extinction diameter from 1.89 mm down to 0, while the hot-flame value stays near 3.5 mm.

studies.title: Bigger droplets lose their hot flame earlier
studies.what: Three fuels at 1 atm. The larger the droplet starts, the larger it still is when the hot flame goes out. In the simulation, 2 mm and 3 mm droplets are listed with an extinction diameter of 0.

studies.title: Extinction diameter against pressure, measured and simulated
studies.what: The same question as the first chart, from the 2024 paper: where the hot flame and the cool flame go out as pressure changes.

studies.title: Cool flames burn fuel faster at higher pressure
studies.what: Average burning rate during the cool-flame stage. Measured values rise from about 0.32 mm²/s at 0.5 atm to about 0.5 mm²/s at 5 atm.

studies.title: One droplet from ignition to burnout at 1 atm
studies.what: A single 4 mm n-dodecane droplet. The droplet shrinks (d² falls) while the flame and its heat output change over time.
warn: Series marked with ? carry no measured/simulated label in the file. The tag was inferred from the column layout; check it against the paper figure.

panels.title: Heat radiated
panels.note: The file does not say what separates series 1 from series 2.

studies.title: Low pressure against high pressure: 0.5 atm and 5 atm
studies.what: Two droplets of about 4.5 mm, one at each pressure, with the matching simulations.

studies.title: A droplet that burns in three stages
studies.what: n-dodecane at 2.75 atm in a helium mix. Time is divided by the starting diameter squared so droplets of different sizes line up.
warn: Series marked with ? carry no measured/simulated label in the file. The tag was inferred from the column layout; check it against the paper figure.

studies.title: A steady cool flame against one that pulses
studies.what: Two simulations of a 0.5 mm n-heptane droplet that differ in oxygen level. One settles into a steady cool flame; the other swings in temperature.

studies.title: When a cool flame is blown out (no ozone)
studies.what: Counterflow flames in a lab. Each point is the stretch rate at which the cool flame went out for a given fuel fraction. Higher means the flame is harder to blow out.
warn: The file does not say whether these values are measured or simulated.

ref.label: C.B. Reuter et al. / Combustion and Flame 179 (2017) 23–32, Fig. 4
